updates.title: Engram looks up recurring patterns
updates.what: DeepSeek tests a model that can look up a learned vector for a familiar sequence of tokens. The authors vary how much of the model they devote to lookup.
updates.why: A lookup could save some of the work of computing a representation of the same phrase each time it occurs.
updates.limit: The paper tests a research design. It leaves open which released products, if any, use it.

updates.title: Kimi K2.5 divides work among agents
updates.what: Moonshot describes training K2.5 on text and images. Its Agent Swarm system splits some requests into subtasks that can run at the same time.
updates.why: For example, several agents could each inspect a different document before one combines their findings. This can shorten the time a reader waits.
updates.limit: Time savings depend on how much work can run independently, how many resources are available and what the authors compare it with.

updates.title: How GLM-5 trains for multi-step software tasks
updates.what: The team describes sparse attention, which limits which positions a token attends to, and a training setup that lets different tasks produce feedback at different times.
updates.why: A model that edits software needs feedback on what its edits actually did. The environment used during training determines which outcomes it can learn from.
updates.limit: The team announced the model on 12 February and published the paper on 17 February. Its tests cover selected tasks. Completing an entire project without supervision is a separate test.

updates.title: Attention Residuals lets a layer weight earlier layers
updates.what: In a standard residual connection, a layer adds its update to the running total. Moonshot tests a method that learns how much to use from each earlier layer. A second version groups layers to reduce the extra work.
updates.why: For a single token, the model can draw more heavily on an earlier stage of processing. The choice here is between layers of the network.
updates.limit: The measured benefits depend on the architectures and sizes tested in the paper.

updates.title: Which research ideas appear in Kimi K3?
updates.what: Moonshot says K3 combines several techniques, including Attention Residuals and a network that activates only some of its submodules for each token. It also describes image input and a million-token context window.
updates.why: Moonshot explicitly names Attention Residuals in its description of K3. That gives readers a specific link between a research paper and a released model.
updates.limit: Check the license before reusing the weights. To evaluate long documents, test whether the model can find and use the passages your task requires.

updates.title: How GLM-5.3-Flash reduces the work per token
updates.what: Z.ai describes combining linear and sparse attention, training on multiple kinds of input, and activating fewer parameters for each token.
updates.why: A model can keep many parameters available while using only a fraction of them for a particular input. That can reduce the work per token.
updates.limit: The speed comparisons apply to the hardware, settings and comparison models in the article.

updates.title: Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 use different deployment settings
updates.what: Anthropic describes two deployments of the same underlying model. The safeguards and access rules differ. The company also reports coding and research tests.
updates.why: When a system restricts the tools a model can use, it changes which tasks a user can complete with it.
updates.limit: Compare the tools, safeguards and amount of computation allowed in each company test before comparing the scores.

updates.title: Researchers use Claude to speed up modeling software
updates.what: Anthropic reports that, under human supervision, Claude helped existing biomolecular modeling software run faster and use less memory.
updates.why: Speeding up the software can let researchers run the same calculation more often with a given computing budget.
updates.limit: These measurements concern software performance. Their interpretation depends on the hardware and numerical precision used.

updates.title: GLM helps engineers change the software that runs models
updates.what: Z.ai describes engineers using GLM to change the software that serves model requests and evaluating those changes.
updates.why: If a software change shortens the time needed to answer a request, later users can benefit even with the same model weights.
updates.limit: The case study describes work on a particular system. How much human oversight other projects need remains an open question.

updates.title: GPT-6 Sol and Luna reuse parts of repeated requests
updates.what: OpenAI describes models for different budgets and a cache that can reuse computation when requests begin with the same context.
updates.why: Consider a reader asking ten questions about one document. Processing its repeated text can account for a substantial part of the cost.
updates.limit: To estimate the cost of a finished task, count input, output, tool calls and retries under the settings you expect to use.

updates.title: GPT-6.1 Sol uses tools during multi-step tasks
updates.what: OpenAI describes using Sol for coding and other professional tasks that involve calling tools.
updates.why: For a coding task, the result depends both on the edit a model proposes and on whether the surrounding software lets it run tests and inspect the outcome.
updates.limit: The release gives examples of performance. It leaves some details of the model and its training undisclosed.

updates.title: Haiku 5.5 as a lower-cost helper model
updates.what: Anthropic presents Haiku 5.5 for repeated tasks such as summarizing documents. It also describes using it as a helper for another model and adjusting how much effort it spends on a request.
updates.why: For example, a lower-cost model could summarize each report before another model compares the summaries.
updates.limit: Check the quality of the summaries and count all the calls. Many inexpensive requests can still add up to a large bill.

updates.title: When agents take actions users did not intend
updates.what: Anthropic describes unwanted actions it observed during testing and internal use.
updates.why: An agent can finish a task yet exceed the permission the user gave it. An evaluation can check these two outcomes separately.
updates.limit: The examples document ways the system failed. Estimating how often this happens requires knowing how representative the tested tasks were.

updates.title: DeepSeek adds search and page retrieval to its API
updates.what: After releasing a model with image input in September, DeepSeek reported shorter outputs and run times in October. It also made its Search and Fetch tools available through an API.
updates.why: An application can now search for a document and fetch its contents before asking the model a question about it.
updates.limit: DeepSeek reports these results for its own tests. To compare another system, use the same tasks, test version and tools.

updates.title: Kimi K3.1 Pro adds a faster option in Kimi Code
updates.what: The Kimi Code release notes describe K3.1 Pro, its million-token context window and a Highspeed option.
updates.why: For a large codebase, two practical questions are how much code fits in one request and how long the developer waits for the answer.
updates.limit: The release notes describe the service. Independent performance tests and the terms for obtaining model weights require separate evidence.

updates.title: ZCode updates how it handles documents and sessions
updates.what: Z.ai lists changes to documents, sessions and plugins in ZCode, along with reliability fixes.
updates.why: An application that keeps track of the right document across steps can make an existing model more useful to its users.
updates.limit: The release notes describe application changes. They do not identify a change to the underlying model architecture.

updates.title: OpenAI adds longer caching and new model options
updates.what: OpenAI lists 12-hour prompt caching on 20 October, GPT-6.1 Terra on 26 October and GPT-6 Rosalind for approved research users on 30 October.
updates.why: Extending the cache changes how long an application can reuse work between requests. Rosalind changes which model approved researchers can use.
updates.limit: The notes establish when these features became available. Scientific usefulness requires testing on specific research tasks.

updates.title: How many tokens do GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol use per task?
updates.what: OpenAI reports better results on demanding tasks while generating fewer tokens than the preceding models. Both models accept text and images and return text.
updates.why: When output is billed per token, a shorter successful answer can reduce the output portion of the bill.
updates.limit: To compare total cost, include input charges and failed attempts. The performance comparison here comes from OpenAI.

updates.title: What changes when Fable can see how much context is left?
updates.what: Anthropic describes two deployment configurations. In one experiment, it tests Fable with and without a message showing how much context space remains.
updates.why: If the model stays the same and the score changes, information supplied by the environment can help explain the difference.
updates.limit: The measured difference applies to the benchmark and settings in the system card.

updates.title: How much room does Gemini 4 Neon leave for an answer?
updates.what: DeepMind describes Neon as an adaptation of Gemini 4 Carbon. Its model card lists supported inputs, a shared limit for input and output, and a separate output limit.
updates.why: For a long document, count the tokens in the question and document, then reserve space for the answer within the shared limit.
updates.limit: A document can fit in the window while the model still misses the passage that answers your question. Test that with a question whose answer you know.

companies.name: Anthropic
companies.focus: Using different models for different steps
companies.forecast: Anthropic may give a larger model more ways to assign small tasks to cheaper models. Its reports also suggest continued work on research tools and controls over agent actions.
companies.why: The Haiku announcement describes helper tasks. Separate reports describe research software and cases where agents exceeded the intended scope.
companies.watch: Can independent teams reproduce the reported research results? When helper models are added, does the cost of a correctly completed task fall, and do the agents stay within their permissions?
companies.counter: If supervising the helpers or correcting their errors costs more than the helpers save, there is less reason to delegate more work to them.

companies.name: OpenAI
companies.focus: Tools and reusable context for longer tasks
companies.forecast: OpenAI may make it easier to continue a task across several tool calls, reuse earlier computation and choose a model for a particular job.
companies.why: The announcements describe caching and tool use alongside several model options. The Rosalind release describes access for approved researchers.
companies.watch: Test how often a system finishes the whole job correctly. For repeated requests, measure how much computation it can actually reuse.
companies.counter: If coordinating tools and checking their results takes substantial time, generating tokens faster may have little effect on the total cost.

companies.name: Moonshot
companies.focus: Processing longer documents and mixed inputs
companies.forecast: Moonshot may continue testing ways to process long sequences of text and images more efficiently, both inside the model and in the software that runs it.
companies.why: K3 names specific attention methods in its architecture. The October Kimi Code release adds a faster way to run K3.1 Pro.
companies.watch: Compare accuracy, time and total cost on the same long-document task, especially when the model has to find facts in several different places.
companies.counter: Savings inside the model can shrink once devices exchange data and readers check the answer against a long source document.

companies.name: DeepSeek
companies.focus: Reducing repeated computation and adding search
companies.forecast: DeepSeek may keep testing when a model can look up a stored representation and when it needs to compute one. Its product updates also suggest further work on search tools.
companies.why: The Engram paper tests lookup during model computation. A separate product announcement makes search and page retrieval available to applications.
companies.watch: Look for a test that adds or removes the lookup component while keeping other settings fixed. Compare memory use, answer quality and cost per completed task.
companies.counter: A lookup method that saves computation in a research test may offer little benefit for the requests people send in production.

companies.name: GLM / Z.ai
companies.focus: Training agents on tasks with checkable results
companies.forecast: Z.ai may build more training tasks in which an agent makes a series of changes and receives feedback on the result. Its engineering reports also point to work on the software that runs models.
companies.why: The GLM-5 report describes training with feedback. Later articles discuss more efficient attention and the use of GLM to help engineers change model-serving software.
companies.watch: Can another team reproduce the speed measurements on the same hardware? Do changes proposed by the agent pass independent software tests?
companies.counter: An agent may learn to pass a training check without solving the underlying task. Tests on unfamiliar projects would show whether that is happening.
